2027-07-30.title: Friday of the tenth week after Pentecost
readings: You are children of the light and of the day: let us keep awake and be sober
At daybreak Jesus goes to a deserted place, and then goes on to proclaim the kingdom to other cities
2027-07-30.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Tenth Sunday after Pentecost. No commemoration is printed in the Panchangam today.
2027-07-30.verse: for you are all children of light and children of the day; we are not of the night or of darkness.
theo: Paul begins this passage by saying that he has no need to write about “the times and the seasons.” The Thessalonians were anxious about when the Lord would return, and some seem to have been neglecting their daily work (compare 2 Thessalonians 3:11). Paul does not give a date. He gives a picture that every household knows: “you yourselves know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.” A thief sends no notice; no one who is ready for him is troubled when he comes. The people who are caught are those who say, “There is peace and security,” and have settled down comfortably on their own foundations, as though nothing could shake the house. We have seen in Kerala how fast a calm monsoon morning can turn into a flood. Security that depends on our own arrangements is thin. The security of the believer is of another kind, and Paul states it as a fact about who we are: “But you, beloved, are not in darkness, for that day to surprise you like a thief; for you are all children of light and children of the day; we are not of the night or of darkness.”

From that identity Paul draws a single instruction: “So then let us not fall asleep as others do, but let us keep awake and be sober.” To keep awake is not to live in fear or to be forever scanning the sky. It means to be alert in the Lord, the opposite of the sleep of routine, in which days pass one after another and nothing is asked and nothing is given. To be sober is to keep a clear head, not dulled by the noise of news, by money or by pleasure. Paul goes on a few verses further to give the reason for the confidence: God “has destined us not for wrath but for obtaining salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep we may live with him.” The Day is not a trap but a meeting with the One who died for us. The early morning, with the first bell of the church, the first fishing boats going out and the first tea stalls opening, is the most natural picture of the Christian life: we live as people who are up before the light because we are expecting someone.

In the Gospel the first one awake is the Lord himself. The evening before, the whole town of Capernaum had crowded around the door with its sick; and now, “at daybreak he departed and went into a deserted place.” The Gospel of Mark tells us what he did there: he prayed (Mark 1:35). When the crowds find him and “wanted to prevent him from leaving them,” he answers, “I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose.” It would have been easy to stay where he was loved and needed. But he lives by his mission, not by popularity, and his mission comes from prayer: before he speaks to the people he speaks to the Father. Christians who keep awake are those who begin the day as he did and then go where they are sent, to the next town, the next ward, the next neighbour. “So he continued proclaiming the message in the synagogues of Judea.” The kingdom is not kept in one village; it goes on.
outline: Ask: am I awake in the Lord, or asleep in routine?
We belong to the day; no thief of the night can surprise those who are ready.
Alertness and a clear head, in confidence that God has destined us for salvation.
He prays in a deserted place, and then goes on to the other cities, for he was sent.
“Let us keep awake and be sober.”
live: Get up ten minutes earlier tomorrow, before the phone and the news, and give those minutes to prayer.
Choose one thing that dulls you, too much news or screen time, and put it aside for one day this week.
2027-07-30.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you rose at daybreak and went to a deserted place to pray, and you went on to the other cities because you were sent. Keep us awake and sober, children of light and of the day. Let no thief of the night find us asleep, and send us where you wish, so that whether we are awake or asleep we may live with you. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the Church keeps vigil for the Lord's coming: we proclaim his death, we confess his resurrection, and we wait in hope for his coming again, awake and sober, as children of the day.

quick: Paul says that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, but we are children of light and of the day.
We should not fall asleep as others do, but keep awake and be sober.
Jesus went out at daybreak to a deserted place to pray, and then went on to proclaim the kingdom in other cities, because he was sent.
2027-07-30.action: Get up a little earlier tomorrow and give the first minutes of the day to the Lord.
2027-07-30.question: Am I awake in the Lord, or asleep in routine?

family.explain: Jesus got up very early in the morning, before everyone else, and went to a quiet place to talk to his Father. The people wanted him to stay with them, but he said, “I have to tell other towns about God's kingdom too.” St Paul says that we are children of the light and of the day. That means we should wake up and be ready to do good, just as Jesus did.
family.intention: We pray for people who work at night and early in the morning, for fishermen, bakers, nurses and drivers.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the first thing I will say to God when I wake up tomorrow?”

illus: A tea-shop owner in a small town near Kuttanad opened his shutter at four every morning, an hour before anyone came. Asked why, he said that he used the hour to sit on his stool and say the morning prayer and the rosary before the first fisherman came to the door. “By the time the first customer comes,” he said, “my heart has had its tea.” The fishermen and the early bus drivers who stopped there said that the shop had a calm that no other tea stall had, and a few of them, who did not even go to church, began to leave their nets on the bench for a moment and say a prayer of their own.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you rose at daybreak to pray. Keep us awake and sober, children of light and of the day. Amen.
share: The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night (1 Thessalonians 5:2). How does this make me feel, afraid or ready?
You are all children of light (1 Thessalonians 5:5). Where do I let my light shine?
I must proclaim the good news to the other cities also (Luke 4:43). Where am I sent today?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us awake in you.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep awake and sober and be faithful to the mission she was sent on.
For those who work at night and early in the morning, that the Lord may protect them.
For those who are tempted to give up hope, that they may hear the words: you are children of the day.
For the sick and the dying, that they may live with the Lord whether awake or asleep.
For ourselves, that we may begin each day with prayer, as the Lord did.
pm.close: Father, you have destined us for salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us. Keep us awake and sober, children of the day, and send us in the strength of prayer to proclaim your kingdom wherever you wish. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells the Thessalonians that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night (1 Thessalonians 5:2). But he does not frighten them. You are not in darkness; you are all children of light and children of the day (1 Thessalonians 5:4–5). A thief surprises the sleeping, not those who are awake.

So the instruction is simple: let us not fall asleep as others do, but let us keep awake and be sober (1 Thessalonians 5:6). To keep awake is not to live in fear. It is to be alert in the Lord, the opposite of the sleep of routine, and to keep a clear head. And the reason for our confidence is that God has destined us not for wrath but for salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for us, so that whether we are awake or asleep we may live with him (1 Thessalonians 5:9–10).

In the Gospel, the first one awake is Jesus himself. At daybreak he went to a deserted place to pray. The crowds wanted to keep him, but he said, I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose (Luke 4:43). His mission comes out of prayer.
So let us rise a little earlier, give the first minutes to the Lord, and then go where we are sent. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know who is awake in the early morning? The farmers, the fishermen, the bakers, the milk sellers, and the birds! Jesus also got up very early in the morning, before everyone else, and went to a quiet place to talk to his Father. Then he went to the next town to tell the people about God. St Paul says that we are children of the light and of the day. So tomorrow morning, when you wake up, say hello to Jesus before you say hello to anyone else. Say, “Good morning, Lord!”

intro: Theme: “You are all children of light and children of the day.”
On Friday of the tenth week after Pentecost: the thief in the night, the call to keep awake and sober, and the Lord who rises at daybreak to pray.

sub: We are not of the night or of darkness.
The day of the Lord comes like a thief.
A thief surprises the sleeping, not the watchful.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
For once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light.
points.apply: Each night this week say: Lord, I am a child of your day; keep me awake in you.

sub: Not fear, but alertness in the Lord.
A clear head in a noisy world.
Destined for salvation, awake or asleep.
q: O Lord, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I plead my case to you, and watch.
And what I say to you I say to all: Keep awake.
points.apply: Give the first ten minutes of the morning to prayer, before the phone and the news.

sub: He rises early and prays in a deserted place.
The crowds want to keep him.
He goes on, for he was sent.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
He answered, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim the message there also; for that is what I came out to do.”
points.apply: Ask the Lord today where you are sent, and go there.

concl: We belong to the day: no thief of the night can surprise those who are awake in the Lord.
The Lord himself rises at daybreak to pray, and then goes where he is sent; we follow him.
2027-07-30.resolve: Keep awake and sober, begin the day in prayer, and go where you are sent.
